exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Gratin dauphinois meets Thanksgiving sweet potatoes - alternating layers of sweet and white potatoes create a dish with more complexity than either alone. Even 1/8-inch slices cook consistently and meld into the cream. Use a sharp knife or a mandoline with its hand guard; thicker slices need more time. Whisking the garlic, herbs and seasonings into the cream distributes them through the layers. Start covered at high heat to cook the potatoes through, then uncover to build the golden crust.

## Directions

1.  **Mix:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Whisk the cream, garlic, thyme, sage, rosemary, nutmeg, cayenne, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
2.  **Slice:** Use a sharp knife or a mandoline with its hand guard to slice all potatoes into 1/8-inch thick rounds. Keep the colors separate for layering.
3.  **Cheese Mix:** Combine the shredded Gruyère and Parmesan in a bowl.
4.  **Layer:** Pour one-sixth of the seasoned cream into a 9x13 baking dish.
    - Layer 1: Sweet potatoes (slightly overlapping). Drizzle with cream, sprinkle with cheese.
    - Layer 2: White potatoes. Drizzle with cream, sprinkle with cheese.
    - Repeat, dividing the cream and cheese among the layers and reserving cheese for the top. Use all of the cream.
5.  **The Crown:** For the top layer, alternate colors for a beautiful visual pattern. Cover with the remaining cheese.
6.  **Bake:** Cover with foil. Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes.
7.  **Crisp:** Remove foil. Reduce heat to 400°F. Bake for about another 45 minutes, until the potatoes are tender throughout when pierced with a knife. If the top browns before the potatoes soften, cover loosely with foil and continue baking.
8.  **Rest:** Let rest for 10 minutes before serving so the layers set.

## Timing

The 95-minute estimate includes 25 minutes of preparation, about 60 minutes of baking and the 10-minute rest. Thicker slices or a deeper dish can take longer; test the center before taking the gratin out.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Kaitlin Gwock’s gratin alternates sweet potatoes and Yukon Golds beneath the full cream and cheese. Keep the slices evenly about 1/8 inch thick. Whisk the seasonings into the cream so every layer gets them; cook until a knife slips through the center layers, and tent the top if it browns first.

## Directions

1. **Mix:** Preheat the oven to 425°F. Whisk all the cream, garlic, thyme, sage, rosemary, nutmeg, cayenne, salt and pepper together.
2. **Slice:** Use a sharp knife or a mandoline with its hand guard to cut the peeled potatoes into even 1/8-inch rounds. Keep the colors separate for layering.
3. **Combine cheese:** Mix all the Gruyère and Parmesan together.
4. **Layer:** For the original batch, use a 9×13-inch oven-safe dish with enough depth for the full potatoes, cream and cheese. If necessary, divide the entire batch among additional dishes before layering, keeping similar depth and headroom. Divide all measured ingredients among the dishes. Pour one-sixth of each dish’s allocated cream over its bottom. Alternate overlapping sweet-potato and white-potato layers, dividing the rest of its cream and cheese through the layers and reserving cheese for its top. Use all the cream; do not leave a fixed-volume remainder behind.
5. **Top:** Arrange the last layer in alternating colors if desired and cover with the reserved cheese.
6. **Start covered:** Cover with foil and bake at 425°F for 15 minutes.
7. **Finish:** Remove the foil and reduce the oven to 400°F. Bake about another 45 minutes, until a knife passes easily through the potato layers in the center of each dish. If the top browns before the potatoes soften, cover loosely with foil and continue checking; thicker slices or deeper layers need longer.
8. **Rest:** Rest for 10 minutes before serving so the layers hold together. Add the optional additional thyme garnish if using it.

## Timing

The original 95-minute estimate includes 25 minutes of preparation, about 60 minutes of baking and the 10-minute rest. Extra loads, thicker slices or deeper dishes can take longer; the center’s tenderness governs.

ingredients: 2 cup finely grated parmesan reggiano cheese
savedOriginal.directions:
Whisk 3 c heavy cream, 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 3 cloves minced garlic, 1 tbsp fresh chopped thyme, 1 tbsp fresh chopped sage, 1 tsp fresh chopped rosemary, 1/4 tsp nutmeg & a dash of cayenne pepper in a large bowl

In a separate bowl mix 2 1/2 c shredded gruyere cheese & 2 c finely grated parmesan reggiano cheese.

Peel 2 lbs of sweet potatoes & 1 1/2 lbs of white potatoes.

Carefully use a handheld mandolin slicer and slice peeled potatoes into thin rounds.

Pour 1/2 c of the cream into the bottom of a casserole dish then neatly layer one layer of the sweet potatoes having them overlap slightly.

Drizzle 3/4 c of cream mixture on top & sprinkle 1 c of cheese on top of that.

Next layer the white potatoes and repeat the steps, then a sweet potato layer repeating the steps.

For the top layer of potatoes layer with both colors & sprinkle all remaining cheese on top and garnish with chopped thyme.

Cover with foil & bake on 425 for 15 minutes until cheese is bubbly.

Remove foil & reduce heat to 400 degrees & bake for 45 minutes until top is golden & bubbly.

Let cool & serve as a Thanksgiving side dish, then EAT!
